newsitem.title: LEBANON: Ownership issue delays Byblos Bank listing.
newsitem.headline: Ownership issue delays Byblos Bank listing.

text.p: Lebanon's Byblos Bank is experiencing a further delay in listing on the Beirut Stock Exchange because of the need to meet a legal requirement that 33 percent of its shares remain in Lebanese hands after trading begins, General Manager Francois Bassil said on Friday.
Byblos, which this week reported a 60 percent increase in profits for 1996, is seen as one of Lebanon's most dynamic banks and the listing is eagerly awaited by the market.
It was originally expected at the end of January or early February but market sources now say the listing could come as late as June.
Byblos is one of four Beirut banks which since December have listed shares or announced plans to list, arousing investor interest in the hitherto lacklustre market.

Speaking to Reuters in a telephone interview, Bassil said the ownership issue arose because at present just over 49 percent of Byblos' shares are held by Byblos Invest Holdings, a Luxembourg company, and only 33 percent are category A shares that must be held by Lebanese.
The bank's shares are divided into A shares, which can only be held by Lebanese, and B shares which can be held by Lebanese or foreigners.

The 30 percent of Byblos' shares to be listed under a law passed last year will be open to purchase by foreigners and Byblos has been discussing with the Bank of Lebanon ways to ensure that 33 percent remain in Lebanese hands through the category A shares.
Bassil said the bank planned to set up a Lebanese holding company that would take over some of the shares from the Luxembourg-owned company.

"In order to maintain 33 percent Lebanese ownership through category A shares we are in the process of forming a holding company owned by Lebanese that will buy some of the Byblos Invest Holdings shares and will make an exchange with Lebanese who hold A shares," Bassil said.
He was replying to a question about a report from a market source that the listing could be delayed another two or three months while the issue is resolved.
Both Bassil and the market source said the issue was purely technical but the source said Byblos would have to hold at least one or two general assemblies of shareholders to resolve it.

Last month another source close to the bank told Reuters the issue would cause only a slight delay in the listing. He expected the shares to be traded by March. However, the market source said it was now likely to be delayed until May or June.
